mechanism: Confirmed as written. Core computes the statistics and then overrides two of them: VersionBitsCache::Info fills result.stats from GetStateStatisticsFor and, when the current state is LOCKED_IN, sets stats->threshold to 0 and stats->possible to false (versionbits.cpp:210-217) -- lock-in is already decided, so there is no threshold left to meet and nothing left that could fail. SoftForkDescPushBack then emits the pair only under `if (info.stats->threshold > 0 || info.stats->possible)` (rpc/blockchain.cpp:1337-1340), so in LOCKED_IN both keys are absent and the statistics object is period, elapsed, count only; in STARTED the override does not run and both keys appear. Ours has the guard but not the override: bl.val:versionbits-statistics (src/validation/versionbits.lisp:308-338) returns the deployment's static threshold and a `possible` computed from (>= (+ count (- period elapsed)) threshold) with no reference to the state at all, and %bip9-deployment's (when (or (plusp threshold) possible) ...) at src/rpc/blockchain.lisp:2530-2537 therefore always passes -- every deployment in the table has a positive threshold (regtest 108, the other four chains 1512/1815). The guard is a faithful transcription of Core's line; what is missing is the assignment two files away that makes it ever fire.
consequence: Kept at S3. The numbers we report are not wrong in themselves -- 108 IS the deployment's threshold and the arithmetic behind `possible` is the same formula Core uses -- they are simply the answers to a question that no longer applies once the period has locked in, and Core deliberately withholds them for that reason. The reader-facing effect is that a client watching an activation sees, for a deployment whose signalling window is settled, a threshold of 108 against a count of 12 and possible: true, which reads as a period still in progress that could still fail; the `status: locked_in` field next to it says otherwise, so a careful reader is not misled, and an automated one keying off status is unaffected. No Core functional test asserts this: rpc_blockchain.py's check_signalling_deploymentinfo_result is guarded by `assert height >= 144 and height <= 287` (rpc_blockchain.py:211) and is only ever called at heights 207 and 287, both of which are STARTED -- at 287 the status is still "started" with status_next "locked_in" -- so its expected dict carries threshold 108 and possible True and matches us. Nothing in test/functional reaches getdeploymentinfo in the LOCKED_IN state (grep for locked_in returns only rpc_blockchain.py:280, the status_next argument), and versionbits_tests.cpp does not exercise Info(). So this is a field-set divergence with no test that catches it and no value acted on: S3.

The STARTED control at height 207 on the same chain returns state :STARTED and statistics (144 108 64 64 T), and there Core emits threshold and possible too, so the divergence is state-specific and not a blanket difference; heights 288 and 299 both show it. fix_shape: Put the override where Core puts it -- between computing the statistics and rendering them -- not in the RPC's guard. The cleanest match is to give bl.val a small Info-shaped wrapper, since Core's override lives in VersionBitsCache::Info and not in GetStateStatisticsFor: have %bip9-deployment call versionbits-statistics as it does now and then, when `current` is :LOCKED-IN, replace threshold with 0 and possible with NIL before the existing (when (or (plusp threshold) possible) ...) guard, which then correctly drops both keys. Do not change versionbits-statistics itself to consult the state: that function is also read by callers who want the raw counting result, and Core keeps GetStateStatisticsFor state-blind for the same reason. If the signalling-string fix (bc10de29) lands first and introduces an Info-style helper returning current state, next state, since, stats and the signalling vector together, fold the override into that helper instead so the two states stay described in one place. Test it at three heights on one chain -- 207 (STARTED: both keys present, threshold 108, possible true), 299 (LOCKED_IN: both keys absent, and the statistics object holds exactly period, elapsed, count), and 432 or later (ACTIVE: no statistics object at all) -- asserting the exact key set of the statistics object rather than individual values, with the STARTED row as the positive control that the assertion can fail.
